title: Customer pilot expansion for Provision-to-Ready automation (Dedicated pool)
creator: Vanessa Ortiz
project: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
description:
## Summary
Run the first external customer expansion using the new Provision-to-Ready automation pipeline for a Dedicated pool. This issue covers selecting the customer, defining success criteria, comms plan (Sales/CS + customer-facing), and a concrete rollback plan.

This is the “week 4” deliverable: 1 customer expansion executed with staged rollout + monitoring.

## Context
We’ve validated the automation in internal/staging pools (ENG-2752). Next step is a controlled customer expansion so we can confirm:
- end-to-end time-to-ready improvements hold under real constraints (region/SKU, customer networking policies, SLA expectations)
- readiness gates (GPU health + network + runtime smoke + perf-canary) prevent bad capacity from entering routing
- manual override/pause/resume is operationally safe under time pressure

## Candidate customer selection criteria
**Must have**
- Expansion (add GPUs) to an existing Dedicated pool (not net-new customer pool)
- Customer can accommodate a planned window (2–4 hours) and agrees to “pilot” terms (best-effort within window, rollback possible)
- Region/SKU that matches what we already exercised in staging (avoid introducing new hardware constraints on the first external run)
- Moderate urgency: important but not a “make-or-break” launch date

**Nice to have**
- Existing strong comms channel via CS (fast approvals)
- Predictable workload so we can validate perf-canary thresholds with minimal debate

## Selected customer (proposed)
**Customer:** HubSpot company record 60522 (mid-market Dedicated customer; currently expanding usage)
**Internal refs:** see Sales/CS notes in HubSpot 60522; related support thread is expected to be SUP-2201 style (ETA updates) if we slip.

**Why this customer:**
- Expansion scope is small/medium (initially +8 GPUs) and within a pre-existing pool
- Customer already asks for clearer readiness validation language; aligns with what we’re shipping
- They can schedule a maintenance window and will keep traffic stable during validation

Owner for final customer confirmation: **Lauren Bishop** (Dedicated PM) + **CS** (via Support thread).

## Success criteria
### Primary (hard)
1) **No customer-visible errors attributable to new capacity entering routing**
   - New capacity must remain out of routing until control plane state = Ready and perf-canary pass.
   - If any intermittent 5xx/latency spikes occur during validation, keep pool out of routing and rollback expansion if needed.

2) **Provision-to-Ready completes within target budget for this pilot**
   - Goal: Ready within **<= 6 hours** from “Requested” for this first customer pilot.
   - Record actual per-stage timing (Provisioning/Imaging/Bootstrapping/Validating).

3) **Operators can recover from a failure without ad-hoc/manual cluster surgery**
   - Use pause/resume + stage re-run where applicable.
   - If manual steps are required, capture them in runbook deltas and follow-up issues.

### Secondary (soft)
- Stage timing telemetry shows clean event sequence with correlation ID and no gaps.
- Clear customer update messages sent at agreed checkpoints (start, mid-way if delay, completion/rollback).

## Comms plan
### Audience
- External: customer technical contact + PM/CS counterpart
- Internal: #eng-infra, #eng-sre (monitoring), Dedicated oncall (routing/control plane), Support (FYI)

### Customer-facing messaging (template)
**T-24h confirmation** (CS sends)
- Confirm window, region, GPU count, and “capacity will not be used until validated” statement.
- Share expected timeline (best-effort) and the two outcomes: Ready (capacity available) vs Rollback (no change).

**Start of window** (CS sends)
- “Expansion initiated; capacity will remain out of service until readiness checks pass.”

**If delayed > 2h** (CS sends)
- Provide stage-level status (e.g., Imaging slow) without deep internals.
- Provide revised ETA and remind that rollback is available.

**Completion**
- If success: “Capacity validated and available.” Include time, region, and confirmation that routing only includes Ready.
- If rollback: “Expansion rolled back; no change to existing capacity.” Include next steps and proposed reschedule.

### Internal comms + responsibilities
- **Pilot captain / decision maker:** Harish Reddy
- **SRE safety + rollback call:** Rafael Mendes (or on-call SRE delegate)
- **Routing/control plane readiness:** Ethan Park + Ravi Menon (on-call coverage)
- **Infra pipeline stage ownership:** Vanessa Ortiz (backup Gabe Wilson)
- **Support liaison:** CS/Support via dedicated Slack thread and linked customer ticket

Internal kickoff post (in #eng-infra) should include:
- customer name/ID, pool ID(s), region, target GPU count
- link to runbook section used, dashboards, and provisioning run correlation ID
- explicit rollback triggers and who can pull them

## Rollback plan
### Rollback triggers
- Any readiness gate fails and cannot be remediated within **60 minutes** (or will require “one-off” manual changes).
- Perf-canary fails thresholds twice consecutively.
- Repeated bootstrap failures with unknown cause (avoid turning pilot into an incident).
- Any sign that new capacity may be entering routing before Ready (treat as P0 safety issue; stop and rollback).

### Rollback actions (ordered)
1) **Ensure routing excludes the pool**
   - Confirm control plane state != Ready (or explicitly set pool to “NotReady/Paused” depending on current API support).
   - Verify routing integration only advertises Ready capacity.

2) **Pause provisioning run** (if stuck/flapping)
   - Use pause/resume controls where available.
   - Capture stage + error classification.

3) **Abort expansion safely**
   - If infra resources were created: follow automation “cancel” path, ensuring idempotency (no duplicate resources).
   - If partial cluster exists: tear down per runbook to return to previous known-good.

4) **Fallback to manual path (only if business-critical and approved)**
   - Requires explicit approval from Vanessa + Rafael.
   - Must be documented in real time in the Slack thread and followed by a postmortem note.

### Post-rollback comms
- Customer: “Rolled back, existing capacity unaffected; we’ll reschedule with fixes.”
- Internal: create/attach an INT ticket with logs and remediation PRs/issues.

## Execution checklist
- [ ] Confirm selected customer + get window scheduled (Lauren + CS)
- [ ] Create/attach customer support ticket for tracking (SUP-xxxx)
- [ ] Verify feature flag rollout posture (staging-only vs prod enablement) and approvals (Connor O’Brien)
- [ ] Preflight: verify quotas, region defaults, and SKU availability
- [ ] Preflight: verify config schema validation passes (or approved break-glass if needed)
- [ ] Preflight: dashboards ready (time-to-ready + stage events) and alerts tuned to avoid noise
- [ ] Run expansion; post correlation ID + stage updates internally
- [ ] On success: capture timestamps + before/after comparison; send completion note
- [ ] On failure: rollback using plan; file follow-ups

## Open questions

- Define exact perf-canary thresholds (p50 latency / throughput floor) for this customer’s SKU/region.
